notes: reading: Alimony follows each model's only or default treatment: the divorce date is not stated. Tax-Calculator and TAXSIM treat it as a post-2018 instrument (not income, not deductible); PolicyEngine's default divorce year makes it pre-2019.
reading: Stated financial assistance from friends or relatives outside the household is a gift, not gross income (26 U.S.C. 102(a)).

reading: The stated health savings account deduction is allowed up to the 26 U.S.C. 223(b) limit of one eligible individual, the head, with self-only coverage for the whole year (Rev. Proc. 2025-19: 4,400 for 2026; Rev. Proc. 2024-25: 4,300 for 2025), plus $1,000 when the head is 55 or older (223(b)(3)). The stated deduction states that the unit has an eligible individual; family coverage, a second eligible spouse and Medicare enrollment are not stated (the board's rule: do not infer coverage). Alternatives: family coverage (8,750 for 2026), or each spouse an eligible individual. policyengine-us takes the stated deduction as given.
the stated health savings account deduction of 9,915.44 exceeds the 26 U.S.C. 223(b) limit; 4,400 is allowed (policyengine-us takes the stated amount)
itemized_notes: reading: Stated charitable gifts go to public charities (170(b)(1)(A) organizations): a private foundation is not stated. Non-cash gifts are ordinary-income property, deductible at the stated amount up to 50% of the contribution base less the cash allowed (170(b)(1)(A), (G)(iii)): no appreciation is stated, so none is capital gain property (170(b)(1)(C)). Cash counts up to 60% (170(b)(1)(G)); from 2026 only the total above 0.5% of the contribution base counts (170(b)(1)(I)). The excess over a ceiling carries forward five years; none is stated as carried in. Tax-Calculator applies its own ceilings (30% for non-cash gifts, 60% in all, after the floor); a note names a difference.

board_exclusion_records.alternative_reading: The prompt lists no hours worked and says to treat unlisted numeric inputs as 0; the reference assumed 40 hours a week, which clears the SNAP work requirement for able-bodied adults without dependents. Under the zero-hours reading the time limit applies, which ends benefits after three countable months unless an exemption or area waiver applies; the alternative value is the engine's zero-hours result, not a certified entitlement. The prompt lists home mortgage interest without saying the mortgaged home is the household's residence; if it is, SNAP counts the mortgage payment, interest included, as a shelter cost (7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(ii)(A)), which is the reading under the alternative value.
board_exclusion_records.unlisted_input: weekly_hours_worked_before_lsr and whether the listed home mortgage interest is on the home the SNAP household occupies
board_exclusion_records.note: Corrected value applies r14_unlisted_weekly_hours_v2_v2 and r15_snap_mortgage_interest_v2 together with every publication convention and upstream fix.
